thread:
kyle: heads up — since ~02:00 UTC we started seeing intermittent model-fetch failures in ap-southeast. ~0.5% of requests are failing with 'getaddrinfo: Name or service not known'. Logs point to DNS lookup failures from model-fetcher pods. anyone on call?

marta: saw the same alerts. LB healthchecks flapped and autoscaler started bouncing pods. my initial gut is egress NAT port exhaustion + negative DNS caching making the window worse.

kyle: dug into one node (node-012): tcpdump shows many repeated A queries to our internal forwarder and a lot of truncated/TC responses. conntrack count is huge, lots of TIME_WAIT. ran: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 120k entries.

irene: can you paste a dig to the internal registry from that node? also check `/etc/resolv.conf` and `systemd-resolve --status`. long service names + search path can hit length/truncation issues.

kyle: `dig @169.254.169.253 internal-model-registry.prod.long-service-name.company.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=2` returned NX a few times then SERVFAILs. `/etc/resolv.conf` is a symlink to systemd-resolved; search list has 5 entries (we concatenate namespace+svc+cluster.local variants). our full FQDNs are often >200 chars after search expansion, suspect the resolver or upstream truncation.

sam: also noticed systemd-resolved negative-cache TTL is 300s by default. when forwarder returns SERVFAIL or REFUSED, systemd caches it and we get repeated misses during windows. on high churn (lots of model pulls) this amplifies.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout model-fetcher v2.3.1 completed on 18 nodes at 02:05 UTC :white_check_mark:

marta: short-term mitigation applied: deployed dnsmasq as a node-local sidecar via a daemonset with `negcache=30` and `cache-size=1000`, and pointed resolv.conf to 127.0.0.1 on affected nodes. we also reduced the search list to 2 entries in the kubelet resolv conf patch for these nodes.

kyle: that patch already improved things — healthcheck failures dropped from ~6/min to ~1/min. still seeing periodic spikes when upstream forwarders reply with SERVFAIL.

irene: long-term proposals: (1) scale forwarders / reduce rate-limiting for internal DNS; (2) split egress SNAT pools per AZ to avoid global port exhaustion when a single node fleet churns; (3) reduce ndots/search-path on workloads that talk to long internal FQDNs; (4) make negative TTL telemetry an SLI and alert.

sam: additional ops tweaks I recommend: expand ephemeral port range `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 65535'`, tune `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`, and consider `tcp_tw_reuse=1` behind a staging test. also add a small circuit-breaker in the fetcher to backoff on DNS SERVFAILs to avoid thundering herd.

marta: i'll keep the dnsmasq daemonset rolling on the affected AZs and open a PR to the runbook with commands and rollback steps.

kyle: thanks — can we also add a small packet capture + dig script to the node-prober that runs on demand so we can correlate DNS error spikes with conntrack/port exhaustion next time?

irene: good idea. i'll coordinate with networking to schedule a follow-up review tomorrow 09:00 UTC to decide forwarder autoscaling and SNAT pool split.

sam: opening the runbook PR and a dashboard for negative-cache spikes now. tagging @networking for visibility. :mag:

kyle: thanks all — leaving the mitigation in place. will update if anything regresses.
